A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same watermarking study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–H support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original image, audio, and joint-modality watermarking experiments, including robustness results, ablations, and statistical validation in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds token-entropy measurements and detection-latency benchmarks in Appendices F.7–F.8.

M1.justification: KGW watermarking, RCC encoder/decoder finetuning and its losses, synchronization, and the audio adaptation remain unchanged. Expanded stratification explanations and suggestions for entropy-aware watermarking do not introduce a revised procedure.

E1.justification: The ImageNet/COCO image evaluations, joint image-text detection, text RCC experiment, and VoxPopuli/Moshi audio coverage are retained. The new entropy and timing analyses use existing models and task domains without adding a distinct data population or attack scenario.

E2.justification: Appendix F.8 newly benchmarks Tree-Ring as a latency comparator; v1 evaluated it for robustness in Table 7. Comparator membership in the existing image, audio, and diffusion-watermark comparisons remains unchanged. Newly discussed concurrent methods are not experimentally compared.

E3.justification: The new entropy analysis uses 20 Chameleon generations per modality. The new timing evaluation measures Taming on one H100 and Tree-Ring on a V100 with default implementation parameters. Existing benchmark protocols are retained; these additions do not establish that earlier experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendix F.7 examines modality differences in next-token entropy and periodic variation with image-token position, adding an analysis of behavior relevant to watermarking. Existing ablations, robustness tests, synchronization cases, and audio analyses are retained; the former audio Appendix F.7 becomes F.9.

E5.justification: Appendix F.5 retains the same 10-seed validation and mean/standard-deviation reporting over 100 runs. The new entropy means and standard deviations describe additional token-distribution results, without changing replication, confidence-interval, significance-testing, or calibration procedures.

E6.justification: Tables 1–8 retain their numerical results. Appendix F.7 adds image/text entropy means of 2.93/0.45, standard deviations of 1.90/0.74, and approximately 32-token periodicity. Appendix F.8 adds approximately 1.3 seconds per image for Taming detection and 1.9 seconds for Tree-Ring, measured on different GPUs rather than under matched conditions.

T1.justification: Appendix E.2 corrects the mathematical description of Figure 10: v1 describes dividing the hypergeometric probability Pg by n_alive, whereas v2 correctly plots P(gamma' = g/n_alive) against g/n_alive. The underlying hypergeometric formula, stratification procedure, and detection test are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: token-level autoregressive image watermarking, RCC finetuning, synchronization, and robust detection with preserved generation quality. Condensing the contribution list does not change their scientific scope.

C2.justification: Appendix F.7 interprets higher image-token entropy and row-wise periodicity as opportunities for more reliable, entropy-aware watermarking. Appendix F.8 adds deployment-efficiency interpretations and optimization suggestions. Appendix B expands the rationale for KGW and the applicability of the components to other schemes; the principal existing limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly states that models as well as code are available, documents hardware and component timings for the new efficiency analysis, and clarifies that crop fractions retain the specified proportion of each side. The unchanged crop illustration supports treating this as clarification, not evidence of a changed implementation. Existing training hyperparameters remain.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a focused discussion of concurrent IndexMark, C-reweight, LBW, WIAR, and autoregressive speech watermarking, distinguishing this work through RCC finetuning, synchronization, and robustness evaluation. DiPmark and the follow-up SyncSeal work are also newly cited. This updates positioning without replacing the existing related-work framework.

P1.justification: v2 condenses the contribution bullets into a paragraph, expands selected explanations, adds acknowledgements, and introduces two appendix subsections. The principal section structure and most prose remain intact, including the retained audio appendix under its new number.

P2.justification: v2 adds the two-panel entropy Figure 19; the former Figures 19–24 remain as Figures 20–25. It revises Figure 10's caption and resizes or relocates several existing figures and tables, including Figure 6 and Tables 5–7. The overall visual design and existing experimental displays are retained.

improvement.justification: The entropy and component-latency analyses make token behavior and computational cost easier to assess. The probability correction, clearer crop specification, and concurrent-work discussion improve precision and context. These are useful but limited gains over an otherwise unchanged method and benchmark record. The H100-versus-V100 timing comparison does not establish a matched-hardware efficiency advantage.
